problem:
The rate at which the population of a particular country grows $P(t),$ after $t$ years, can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}P}{\text{d}t}=0.02P.
$$

How many years does it take for the population to double? Round your answer to the nearest year.

feedback.problem:
The rate at which the number of independent mobile applications on a digital marketplace grows $A(t),$ after $t$ years, can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=0.35A.
$$

How many years does it take for the number of applications to triple? Round your answer to the nearest year.
feedback.worked_solution:
We model the growth in the number of applications using the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=0.35A.
$$

The solution to this equation is

$$
A(t)={A}_{0}\,{e}^{0.35t},
$$

where ${A}_{0}$ is the initial number of applications.

Let ${t}_{1}$ be the time when the number of applications is triple the initial number. That is,

$$
A({t}_{1})=3{A}_{0}.
$$

We solve the above equation for ${t}_{1},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A({t}_{1}) & ={A}_{0}{e}^{0.35{t}_{1}} \\ 3{A}_{0} & ={A}_{0}{e}^{0.35{t}_{1}} \\ 3 & ={e}^{0.35{t}_{1}} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡3 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{0.35{t}_{1}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡3 & =0.35{t}_{1} \\ {t}_{1} & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{0.35} \\ {t}_{1} & ≈3.139\end{aligned}
$$

Rounding to the nearest integer, we conclude that it takes $3$ years for the number of applications to triple.
